subtitle: In the Shadow of Sum-tsek: How Anonymous Hands Painted a World

panels.shot: wide, slightly low-angle view of Tashi standing in the dark interior of the Sum-tsek, tiny against towering painted bodhisattvas glowing in lamplight
panels.action: Tashi of Alchi, a robed painter with soot-dusted hands, looks up in awe at the colossal painted bodhisattvas that rise above him inside the Sum-tsek temple, their garments shimmering with intricate patterns in the dim, golden light.

dialogue.text: In a quiet Ladakhi valley, Alchi’s walls blaze with a lost world’s colors, while legend and scholarship still argue who the painters were.

i18n.hi: शांत लद्दाखी घाटी में अलची की दीवारें खोई हुई दुनिया के रंगों से जल उठती हैं, पर कहानी और शोध आज भी झगड़ते हैं कि चित्रकार कौन थे।

panels.shot: high, sweeping aerial over the lower Indus valley, river curving past fields towards a cluster of temples on a rocky terrace
panels.action: The camera floats above the lower Indus valley, where a ribbon of water cuts through brown mountains and green fields, ending at a rocky outcrop crowned by a modest cluster of whitewashed temples and houses.

dialogue.text: Far from imperial courts, on a ledge above the Indus, a small village called Alchi quietly gathered the arts of half a continent.

i18n.hi: दरबारी शानोशौकत से दूर, सिन्धु के ऊपर एक चट्टान पर, अलची नाम का छोटा गाँव चुपचाप आधे महाद्वीप की कलाएँ समेट लाया।

panels.shot: mid-shot inside a dim workshop, side light catching Tashi grinding pigment beside other artisans
panels.action: Inside a low, smoke-darkened room, Tashi of Alchi kneels by a stone slab, grinding mineral pigment as other artisans mix clay and trace lines on primed wooden panels leaning against the wall.

dialogue.text: Here, between about the eleventh and thirteenth centuries, anonymous workshops of painters and sculptors turned clay, cloth and wall into galaxies of Buddhas.

i18n.hi: यहीं, ग्यारहवीं से तेरहवीं सदी के बीच, बेनाम चित्रकारों और मूर्तिकारों ने मिट्टी, कपड़े और दीवारों को बुद्धों की आकाशगंगाओं में बदल दिया।

panels.shot: close-up on Tashi’s hands mixing pigments, with bowls of deep blues, reds and greens visible
panels.action: A tight focus frames Tashi’s hands as he tips powdered lapis, red ochre and malachite into small bowls, adding liquid and stirring until the colors deepen and shine.

dialogue.text: Their palette was not simple village craft. Kashmiri finesse, Pala grace from eastern India, Tibetan forms and Central Asian flourishes all met in these bowls.

i18n.hi: इनके रंग बस गाँव की कारीगरी नहीं थे। कश्मीरी नफ़ासत, पूरब की पाला नज़ाकत, तिब्बती रूप और मध्य एशियाई अदा सब एक ही प्याले में घुल मिले।

panels.shot: wide interior of the Sum-tsek, looking up from floor level at three giant clay bodhisattvas rising through the wooden galleries
panels.action: From the temple floor, the camera looks up to three colossal clay bodhisattvas that rise through wooden galleries, their serene faces level with the rafters and their painted garments cascading in patterned folds.

dialogue.text: The Sum-tsek, Alchi’s three-storeyed marvel, carried an innovation: huge clay bodhisattvas whose very robes became canvases for entire painted worlds.

i18n.hi: अलची का तीन-मंज़िला कमाल सुमत्सेक एक नई बात लाया: महाकाय मिट्टी के बोधिसत्त्व, जिनके वस्त्र ही पूरे चित्रित लोक बन गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Tashi perched on scaffolding, brush poised over a bodhisattva’s robe panel filled with miniature scenes
panels.action: Tashi balances on wooden scaffolding, leaning close to the broad painted robe of a bodhisattva, where he carefully outlines tiny seated Buddhas and dancers within each patterned panel.

dialogue.speaker: Tashi of Alchi
dialogue.text: A single fold must hold a whole realm.

i18n.hi: एक ही सिलवट में पूरा लोक समाना था।

panels.shot: montage-like wide panel showing three contrasting styles on one wall: Kashmiri-style faces, Pala-like mandalas, Tibetan donors
panels.action: A long wall shows different zones: delicate Kashmiri-style oval faces, dense circular mandalas in the Pala manner, and a row of Tibetan donors in layered robes, hands folded, at the base.

dialogue.text: On one wall, sharp-eyed viewers can trace the journey: Kashmiri faces, Pala mandalas, Tibetan patrons, all held together by a Himalayan hand.

i18n.hi: एक दीवार पर तेज़ नज़रें सफर पहचान लेती हैं: कश्मीरी चेहरे, पाला मंडल, तिब्बती दाता, सबको थामे एक हिमालयी हाथ।

panels.shot: close-up of a stone inscription panel in the temple, chisel marks visible, with faint donor text lines
panels.action: The camera lingers on a stone inscription set into the temple wall, the chisel cuts still crisp, the lines of Tibetan script running in even rows beneath a simple border.

dialogue.text: The walls also speak in stone. Dedicatory inscriptions name donors and teachers, and hint at the layered history of the monument.

i18n.hi: दीवारें पत्थर में भी बोलती हैं। दानपत्र शिलालेखों में दाताओं और आचार्यों के नाम हैं, जो स्मारक की तह-दर-तह कहानी की झलक देते हैं।

panels.shot: cutaway to a stylized parchment map of the Western Himalaya, arrows from Kashmir, Bengal, Tibet converging on Alchi
panels.action: A parchment-like map shows Kashmir, eastern India, and Tibet, with painted arrows curving from each region toward a marked dot in the lower Indus valley labeled only by a small temple icon.

dialogue.text: Trade routes and patronage networks carried artists and ideas along the Western Himalaya, making villages like Alchi crossroads of Buddhist art.

i18n.hi: व्यापार मार्ग और संरक्षण की डोरें कलाकारों और विचारों को पश्चिमी हिमालय में ले चलीं, और अलची जैसे गाँव बौद्ध कला के चौराहे बन गए।

panels.shot: dramatic transition shot: half in warm tones showing medieval artists at work, half in cooler tones showing later Ladakhi monks maintaining the temple
panels.action: The frame is divided: on one side, medieval artisans on scaffolds paint; on the other, centuries later, Ladakhi monks in heavy robes sweep the same floor and light lamps before the murals.

dialogue.text: Long after the first workshops fell silent, Ladakhi communities and, later, Namgyal rulers kept Alchi within their sacred landscape, preserving and reinterpreting its art.

i18n.hi: पहली कार्यशालाएँ चुप पड़ जाने के बहुत बाद भी, लद्दाखी समाज और फिर नामग्याल राजाओं ने अलची को अपने पवित्र परिदृश्य में जोड़े रखा, उसकी कला को बचाया और नए अर्थ दिए।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Ladakhi monk of a later century standing before the murals, gesturing as if teaching younger monks
panels.action: A later-era Ladakhi monk stands before a wall of bodhisattvas, one hand raised as he explains the scenes to a small group of seated novice monks inside the cool, dim temple.

dialogue.text: By the time the Namgyal dynasty rose in Ladakh, these paintings were already old, yet they remained living scriptures in color.

i18n.hi: जब तक लद्दाख में नामग्याल वंश उभरा, ये चित्र पहले ही पुराने हो चुके थे, पर रंगों में लिखी ये आयतें तब भी ज़िंदा थीं।

panels.shot: close-up on a modern printed book open on a scholar’s lap, showing a photograph of Alchi murals with caption mentioning Rinchen Zangpo
panels.action: Modern hands hold open a glossy art book with a photograph of the Sum-tsek interior; below, a caption links the temple to the famous translator Rinchen Zangpo.

dialogue.text: Later tradition, carried into modern books, wove Alchi into the story of the great translator Rinchen Zangpo, making him the easy answer to who built and painted it.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा, जो आधुनिक किताबों तक पहुँच गई, ने अलची को महान अनुवादक रिनचेन ज़ांगपो की कथा में पिरो दिया, मानो वही इसके निर्माता और चित्रकार हों।

panels.shot: medium shot of a present-day scholar in a study, surrounded by photographs and rubbings of inscriptions from Alchi
panels.action: A present-day scholar sits at a cluttered desk, comparing black-and-white photographs of Alchi murals and close-up images of inscriptions spread around a laptop.

dialogue.text: But recent scholars returned to the walls themselves, reading the dedicatory texts and the style, and found a more complex timeline.

i18n.hi: पर नए विद्वान लौटा सीधे दीवारों की ओर, दानपत्र पढ़े, शैली परखी, और एक कहीं ज़्यादा उलझा हुआ समयक्रम निकाला।

panels.shot: split shot contrasting a romanticized painting of Rinchen Zangpo supervising artists with a question mark dissolving over it, and the real murals alongside
panels.action: On one side, a romantic image shows a saintly Rinchen Zangpo directing painters; on the other, the actual Alchi murals are shown in detail, while a translucent question mark fades over the imagined scene.

dialogue.text: Christian Luczanits and others argue that major murals likely postdate Rinchen Zangpo, pointing instead to later workshops rather than a single saintly founder.

i18n.hi: क्रिस्टियान लुचज़ानित्स और दूसरे मानते हैं कि मुख्य भित्ति-चित्र शायद रिनचेन ज़ांगपो के बाद के हैं, और इशारा बाद की कार्यशालाओं की ओर करते हैं, न कि किसी एक पवित्र संस्थापक की ओर।

panels.shot: close-up on a highlighted line of an inscription rubbing, with a scholar’s finger tracing the script
panels.action: A scholar’s finger gently traces a particular line on a paper rubbing of an Alchi inscription, the focused light picking out the raised Tibetan characters.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions name donors and teachers, yet the painters remain unnamed, their identities folded into the collective devotion of their patrons’ age.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख दाताओं और आचार्यों को नाम से पुकारते हैं, पर चित्रकार बेनाम ही रहते हैं; उनकी पहचान उनके ज़माने की सामूहिक भक्ति में घुल मिल गई।

panels.shot: soft-focus blend shot of Tashi painting, overlaid faintly with a modern conservationist carefully cleaning a mural
panels.action: Tashi leans toward the wall with his brush in mid-stroke, while, ghostlike in the same frame, a modern conservator in gloves delicately cleans the same painted area with a swab.

dialogue.text: Today, conservators and historians work under the same silent figures, not to uncover a single heroic name, but to let the paintings themselves keep speaking.

i18n.hi: आज संरक्षक और इतिहासकार उन्हीं खामोश पुतलों के नीचे काम करते हैं, किसी एक नायक का नाम खोजने नहीं, बल्कि इन चित्रों को खुद बोलते रहने देने के लिए।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Alchi complex at dusk, a few visitors and monks moving quietly, mountains darkening around
panels.action: At dusk, the small cluster of Alchi temples glows softly against the darkening mountains, a few visitors and monks moving in hushed lines between doorways as prayer flags stir in the evening wind.

dialogue.text: Placed on UNESCO’s tentative list, Alchi now stands as part of a wider Himalayan heritage, linking villagers, pilgrims and scholars around its painted halls.

i18n.hi: यूनेस्को की अस्थायी सूची में जुड़कर अलची अब व्यापक हिमालयी धरोहर का हिस्सा है, जो गाँव वालों, तीर्थयात्रियों और विद्वानों को उसकी रंगी दीवारों के इर्द-गिर्द जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Tashi’s face lit by lamplight as he looks back over his finished mural, eyes tired yet calm
panels.action: By lamplight, Tashi steps back from a completed mural, his lined face calm and tired as he studies the rows of Buddhas and bodhisattvas glowing faintly in the flicker.

dialogue.speaker: Tashi of Alchi
dialogue.text: Names will fade. Color may endure.

i18n.hi: नाम मिट जाएँगे। शायद रंग टिक जाएँ।

panels.shot: final wide interior shot of the Sum-tsek with no people, camera slowly pulling back from the painted giants into darkness
panels.action: The Sum-tsek interior is empty, the camera receding from the towering bodhisattvas whose robes are crowded with tiny worlds, until the forms fade into shadow and only their silhouettes remain.

dialogue.text: Alchi’s painters kept their secret well: they left us no names, only a demand that our wonder be honest enough to follow the evidence wherever it leads.

i18n.hi: अलची के चित्रकारों ने अपना राज़ खूब बचाए रखा: वे नाम छोड़ गए नहीं, बस ये उम्मीद कि हमारा विस्मय इतना सच्चा हो कि सबूत जिधर ले जाए, हम उधर चलें।

title_i18n.hi: अलची ने चित्रकारों का राज़ छुपा रखा है

subtitle_i18n.en: In the Shadow of Sum-tsek: How Anonymous Hands Painted a World
subtitle_i18n.hi: सुमत्सेक की छाया में: अनजान हाथों ने गढ़ी एक रंगी दुनिया
